title: Lesson 1: Running a Full Engagement
description: Turning the five-phase lifecycle into a week-by-week plan: mapping discover, design, implement, handover, and support onto a real calendar, with gates, buffers, and the scheduling realities that kill engagements.

questions.question: What should set the length of each phase when a multi-week plan is built?
options: The time needed to reach its gate
A fixed allotment of weeks per phase
The order the phases are listed in
questions.explanation: Each phase ends at a gate, so its length is however long it takes to satisfy that gate, not a preassigned block of weeks.

questions.question: Which force most directly limits how fast discovery and design can move?
options: The number of tools and data sources the delivery touches
The model selected for each scheduled task
How fast the client's stakeholders respond
The size of the implementation backlog
questions.explanation: Stakeholders who must answer questions and approve scope control the pace, so review gates should be scheduled around their calendar, not the consultant's.

questions.question: When a plan is sized for a client build, how should review cycles be treated?
options: As a formality that costs almost no calendar time
As a single pass that runs only at the end
As a small step absorbed into the build effort
As a bottleneck to plan several cycles for
questions.explanation: The show, feedback, and revise loop eats real calendar time, so a plan should assume more than one review cycle rather than a single pass.
